clue.text: Soft rabbit eating too much

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: cony is an old word for a rabbit
OTT is short for over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: A rabbit gorging itself until it goes soft and flabby.
explanation.walkthrough: The rabbit here is an archaic word for one, still common in crosswords, and the excess sits inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with the texture of cotton wool is fluffy and yielding to the touch.

clue.text: Surgery on broken 24d is best

indicators.note: something broken has its parts knocked out of their proper order

blocks.note: OP is short for operation
the answer to 24 down, used as letters

explanation.surface: A medical note that surgery is the best option for a broken limb.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 24d stands for TAMIL, whose letters are rearranged after the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the most favourable or advantageous choice available.

clue.text: Cat ultimately getting into row

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is wanted
going into something puts one piece within the other

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A cat finally squeezing itself into a row of seats.
explanation.walkthrough: A tier is one of a rising series of rows, as in a stadium; G slips between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the largest member of the cat family, a striped big cat.

clue.text: Canute’s messed up fruitcake

indicators.note: something messed up has been thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the king's name with its S

explanation.surface: King Canute botches a fruitcake, perhaps in the royal kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' looks like the baked kind, but here it is the slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal slang terms for someone eccentric or mentally unbalanced.

clue.text: Nazis inspiring rubbish bands

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside another

blocks.note: the SS was a Nazi paramilitary organisation
tripe means nonsense

explanation.surface: Nazis whose ideas inspired some terrible music groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests musicians, but it means strips of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow strips of colour differing from the surrounding surface.

clue.text: Leg got injured in fastener

indicators.note: something injured has been knocked out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the two words as written

explanation.surface: Someone hurt their leg after getting caught in a fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' reads as describing the leg, but it tells you to rework the letters of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A toggle is a short wooden peg sewn on a coat and pushed through a loop to close it.

clue.text: Unions prepared to accept old copper is harmless

indicators.note: to prepare is to make ready by arranging, so the letters are rearranged
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Trade unions ready to take back an old policeman, a harmless decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something not likely to cause injury, offence or damage.

clue.text: Journalist following Wimbledon champion gets turned inside out

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, setting the order of the pieces

blocks.note: Chris Evert won the Wimbledon singles three times
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter trailing a tennis champion gets their story turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Evert was an American tennis star of the 1970s and 80s.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert is the technical verb for flipping an organ or a structure so its interior faces outward.

clue.text: Wealthy lady’s chauffeur taking A-road for 3

indicators.note: one thing taking another has it alongside, so the pieces sit together

blocks.note: a synonym
A as written, then RD as the abbreviation for road
Parker drives Lady Penelope in the TV puppet series Thunderbirds

explanation.surface: A rich woman's driver taking a main road on her behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference to 3 down, TIGER. Parker is Lady Penelope's chauffeur in the 1960s puppet show Thunderbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Parker is the Bengal tiger sharing the lifeboat in Yann Martel's novel Life of Pi.

clue.text: Male has time to stop droop

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece is wedged inside another

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a synonym

explanation.surface: A man taking time out to stop his body drooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male' looks like it describes a person, but it is the definition, an adult male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and the word also means an all-male gathering.

clue.text: Lofty marksman to follow Arsenal player

blocks.note: to tail someone is to follow them
Arsenal football club are nicknamed the Gunners

explanation.surface: A tall striker set to join Arsenal.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club whose nickname is the Gunners. 'Lofty' is not tall; it means up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail gunner shoots from the rear turret of a bomber aircraft, so is a marksman high in the sky.

clue.text: A drink from the East River

indicators.note: reading from the east in an across entry means going right to left, the opposite way

blocks.note: taken as written
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A spirit imported from the East to the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amur is a long river forming part of the border between Russia and China.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amur is a major river of northeast Asia, flowing into the Pacific.

clue.text: Lucy Liu’s first hit about footballers

indicators.note: the first of something is its opening, so only the initial letter is kept
about can mean all around and in disorder, so the letters are turned every which way

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the surname
taken as written

explanation.surface: The actress Lucy Liu's first hit film, about a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like a box-office success, but it simply supplies three letters to be mixed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hull City is an English professional football club, so its players are footballers.

clue.text: One not listening to Charles rambling

indicators.note: rambling wanders without a fixed route, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: the two words as written

explanation.surface: Someone tuning out while Charles goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth-ears is British informal slang for a person who fails to hear or pay attention to what is said.

clue.text: Cockney criminals make getaway in SEAT hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up
in places one piece within another

blocks.note: to leave is to depart
taken as written

explanation.surface: East End crooks escaping in a SEAT hybrid car.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAT is a Spanish car maker, so 'hybrid' reads as a car type. In Cockney rhyming slang 'tea leaf' rhymes with thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes, so tea leaves stand for thieves.

clue.text: 3 of clubs?

blocks.note: surface reading: a playing card, the three of clubs
setter's reading: 3 down is TIGER, and the golfer named Tiger shares his surname with a kind of golf club

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference turns the playing card into a golfer's name: Tiger of the clubs used to drive long distances.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is a champion golfer, and woods are long-distance golf clubs with large heads.

clue.text: Prince Harry initially somewhat open to return

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used
returning means going back the way you came, so the order runs backwards

blocks.note: the first letter of the name
a door ajar is slightly open

explanation.surface: Prince Harry seems a little open to returning to royal life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince Harry' reads as one name, but 'Prince' is the definition and 'Harry' only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajah is an Indian king or prince, the title used by rulers of princely states.

clue.text: Letters represented genuine class from Alec Guinness?

definitions.text: Letters represented genuine class from Alec Guinness?

blocks.clueFragment: Letters represented genuine class from Alec Guinness?
blocks.note: surface reading: the actor writing letters showing true class

blocks.clueFragment: Letters represented genuine class from Alec Guinness?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the letters of 'genuine class' can be rearranged into the actor's name, and the answer names that wordplay device

explanation.walkthrough: Check it: GENUINE CLASS and ALEC GUINNESS use exactly the same thirteen letters, which is the point of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a word or phrase formed by rearranging all the letters of another one.

clue.text: Looks around the borders of Singapore for peacemakers

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps another
borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: looks, as in seems
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing Singapore's frontiers in search of peace negotiators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks' is not glances but seems, as in 'he looks tired'.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeasers try to keep peace by conceding to demands, so they are peacemakers of a sort.

clue.text: Urgent introduction to intercourse welcomed by old man

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is used
a guest welcomed is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: ex means former
its first letter
short for gentleman

explanation.surface: An older man eagerly receiving a pressing romantic advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' looks like one unit, a father or husband, but it splits into two words, with the single letter welcomed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something pressing that demands immediate attention.

clue.text: Potato cake containing American and English potato

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: rösti is a Swiss fried cake of grated potato
A is the abbreviation for American
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A potato cake made with American and English potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' here means placed after: E follows the filled cake. A roastie is British slang for a roast potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A roastie is an informal British word for a single roast potato.

clue.text: Panic about uniform revealing bust perhaps

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: to be in a state is to be in a panic
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Alarm at a uniform that shows off the wearer's bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' suggests a chest, but here it is a sculpture of head and shoulders, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpted head and shoulders, one kind of carved or cast figure.

clue.text: Perhaps 3 more ordered by mum

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces are placed next to each other

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
neater means tidier

explanation.surface: Things perhaps arranged more neatly by mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference to 3 down, TIGER, with 'perhaps' showing the tiger is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Some tigers become notorious for attacking and killing people, the classic example of the dangerous predator.

clue.text: Cook dropping starter and side

indicators.note: dropping the starter means losing the opening letter

blocks.note: to steam is a way to cook

explanation.surface: A chef leaving out the first course and the side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' and 'side' sound like courses of a meal; 'side' is a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a side is one of the opposing groups of players.

clue.text: Sri Lankan capital’s temperature rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: The temperature is going up in Colombo, Sri Lanka's chief city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' seems to mean Colombo, but it is a different country's capital entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are an ethnic group of northern and eastern Sri Lanka and southern India.

clue.text: Dick Emery on vacation kidnapped by short pirate

indicators.note: vacating a place empties it, so the middle goes and only the outer letters stay
short means cut off, so the final letter is lost
someone kidnapped is held inside by the captor

blocks.note: the first and last letters
a privateer was a licensed pirate ship or captain

explanation.surface: The comedian Dick Emery, on holiday, is seized by a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a British TV comedian; 'Dick' is cut off to be the definition. The shortened pirate loses its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is old American slang for a detective, and a private eye is a private detective.

clue.text: Winger from United going missing in opening

indicators.note: something going missing is lost, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in team names
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: A football winger disappearing from Manchester United at the start of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' is a footballer on the surface but a winged insect in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A moth is a flying insect, and anything with wings can be called a winger in crosswords.

clue.text: Drunk mothers in Slough

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

blocks.note: ma is mother, so mothers are mas
to slough is to shed, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: Mothers getting tipsy in the English town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is the verb meaning to cast off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is informal slang for very intoxicated after heavy drinking.

clue.text: Lecturer’s cycling becoming obsessive?

indicators.note: a cycle goes round, so a letter moves from one end to the other

blocks.note: a lecturer is a talker, plus the S

explanation.surface: A lecturer who cycles everywhere gets fixated on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests riding a bike; here the last letter goes round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is a person with an unhealthy fixation who persistently pursues someone, an obsessive.
